title: Arm-Based Chips Now Power Over Half of Top Hyperscaler Servers

tickers.name: Arm Holdings plc American Depositary Shares
Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The cloud infrastructure presence of Arm's processors has expanded to more than 50% of servers at major hyperscalers, up from 15% in 2024. The company said it expects that share to exceed 60% by the end of 2026 as platforms from Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia increase their usage of its architecture. In a first for the company, Arm's partners also shipped more than 10 billion chips in a single quarter.

For the second quarter, Arm posted revenue of $1.44B and adjusted earnings per share of 52 cents, beating analyst estimates of $1.38B and 47 cents. Licensing and other revenue grew 50% year-on-year to $773M, though royalty revenue fell to $670M from $715M in the previous quarter. Arm provided a revenue guide for the third quarter between $1.49B and $1.59B.

The chip designer is also diversifying its hardware reach, noting that Arm-based PCs now make up about 20% of global shipments. The company also maintained its guidance on the Arm AGI CPU, citing a potential revenue opportunity of up to $2B across fiscal 2027 and 2028, though it has only secured supply for $1B of that total.

ARM $ARM SAYS ARM-BASED CHIPS NOW RUN MORE THAN HALF OF SERVERS AT THE TOP HYPERSCALERS

Arm says its server share at the biggest cloud providers more than tripled, from 15% in 2024 to more than 50% in 2025, and it expects more than 60% by the end of 2026 as Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt and NVIDIA platforms ramp. Data center royalties doubled from a year ago.

Partners also shipped more than 10 billion Arm-based chips in a single quarter for the first time, and Arm-based PCs are now about 20% of global shipments.

selectedTweets.text:
Arm reports today. if you follow it but haven't read the filings, here's what's changed and what to watch.

$ARM used to be simple. it designs chips, licenses them, and collects a small fee on every chip shipped. most for phones

but now servers are doing the lifting. Royalties grew 22% last quarter to $715M, but data center royalties more than doubled. Arm's server cores (Neoverse) passed 1.5B shipped. 

the first 1B took six years, and the last 500M took nine months.

Arm makes more per chip. Newer designs (Armv9, and its ready-made compute subsystems) carry higher royalty rates. so royalties can grow even when phone volumes are flat. 

the big change lately is that Arm now sells its own chip. the Arm AGI CPU launched in March. In July, Arm said customer demand tops $2B through early 2028, but it has only secured supply for $1B. that's a nice problem to have, but it's still a problem.

it's also a little awkward. Arm's customers are also its competitors now. $QCOM just announced its own Arm-based data center CPU. Selling chips makes Arm a bigger business, and it also means it's competing with the companies paying it royalties.

The guide for this quarter is ~$1.38B in revenue, plus or minus $50M.

What I'd watch on the call later:
- did Arm lock in more chip supply, or is half the demand still a waitlist?
- is it still giving a number for data center royalties, or just saying "strong"?
- do any licensees push back on Arm selling its own silicon?

selectedTweets.text:
OMG!!! $ARM beat on revenue beat on EPS by 11%, and guided above the Street again.

Royalties were the soft spot at $670m, down from $715m last quarter. That's the phone market imo memory costs are squeezing handset builds and Arm collects a little on every chip inside them. 

Everyone knew this was coming and mgmt already trimmed its royalty outlook last quarter.

Everything else made up for it. Licensing came in around $770m which tells you customers are still signing up for Arm's next gen designs, especially for AI and data centers. 

Data center royalties have been doubling, and Arm's own AGI CPU already has more than $2bn of demand.

In our view, phones are the past of this story and the data center is the future. 

Arm is going from collecting a small fee on every chip to selling the chip itself, and that's a much bigger business. Overweight, $500 PT.
